scores.claim_text: Long-standing JDA with BMW (since 2016/2017); JDA was amended September 2024 to extend until certain development milestones, with BMW termination rights beginning Dec 31, 2025; BMW i7 test vehicle May 2025.
scores.supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (cik=BMW NA -- not a US filer; BMW Group files as foreign issuer with partial EDGAR coverage). Self-disclosed amendments show repeated extensions and a termination-rights clause active as of 2025-12-31. BMW related-party revenue collapsed from $5.41M (2024) to $0.189M (2025) per Note on Related Party Transactions.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='Solid Power' (all 10-K/20-F since 2024) returned 48 hits, ALL of which are Solid Power's own filings -- zero external counterparty corroboration in EDGAR.
scores.M_value: 48 EDGAR 10-K/20-F hits, 0 external; BMW is foreign filer (UNVERIFIABLE per Layer 3 Rule 7 caveat); related-party BMW revenue fell 96% YoY ($5.41M -> $0.189M).
scores.interpretation: JDA itself is real (signed 2017+) and BMW retains board seat + >5% stake. But Stage Ladder: still JDA / R&D-license stage, no SOP. Termination rights now active. 96% YoY collapse in BMW-related revenue + i7 'test vehicle' (demonstration, not production) signals deceleration. Apply Calibration Heuristic 3 with extra weight: this is a JDA, not a series-production deal -- and trending backwards. Foreign-issuer caveat tempers from RED to MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: Ford JDA extended again Dec 31 2025 'in connection with winding up of cell development activities,' expected to expire March 31, 2026.
scores.supports: Self-disclosed -- the company itself acknowledges Ford is winding down. EDGAR fulltext on Ford CIK 0000037996 for 'Solid Power' shows only 1 hit, an 8-K from 2021-05-26 (the original announcement). No subsequent Ford 10-K mentions Solid Power.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='Solid Power' cik='0000037996' = 1 hit (2021 8-K only).
scores.M_value: Ford EDGAR mentions of Solid Power: 1 (announcement 8-K 2021). Zero in Ford 10-K filings. Ford was previously a >5% holder; now winding down cell-development side of JDA.
scores.interpretation: This is a HARD CONTRADICTION to the original 2021 design-win narrative. Ford was one of two flagship OEM JDA partners (along with BMW). The cell-development JDA is being wound up; the company is left hoping to 'pursue opportunities to supply Ford with our electrolyte material' post-expiration -- aspirational, not contracted. Per Layer 3 Rule 7, Ford 10-K silence on the relationship after 2022 + explicit wind-down acknowledgment = RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE for the design-win thesis.

scores.claim_text: SK On Agreements: $20M R&D license (2024-2027 milestones), $22M line installation, electrolyte supply >=8MT through 2030 (~$8.3M).
scores.supports: SK On is a private Korean Tier-1 battery maker (SK Group subsidiary), NOT a US SEC filer. EDGAR fulltext for 'SK On' returns 75 hits but no SK On 10-K/20-F exists. SK On invested $30M directly into SLDP at de-SPAC closing in 2021 (per filing). Filing reports concrete progress: FAT completed; SAT 'substantially complete' Q1 2026 expected. Collaborative revenue $15.8M (2025) primarily from SK On Agreements.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='SK On' -> 75 hits but no SK On primary filer. No 20-F or 10-K cross-check available -- foreign private subsidiary.
scores.M_value: SK On not an SEC filer; no counterparty corroboration available through EDGAR. Per cohort metadata Layer 3 Rule 7: foreign-issuer caveat -> UNVERIFIABLE rather than false-clean. However, 2025 collaborative revenue ($15.8M) is meaningfully accruing, and direct SK On payments are documented.
scores.interpretation: Stage ladder: line-installation + R&D license + supply for line validation -- explicitly NOT for commercial cell production (R&D license is contractually limited). 8MT through 2030 is tiny -- ~1.3MT/yr -- not commercial scale. UNVERIFIABLE label correct: revenue is real but counterparty is a foreign non-filer, and the contract language itself limits this to validation/R&D, NOT SOP. Also: $30M SK On equity investment at de-SPAC (Calibration Heuristic 4 -- investment != design win).

scores.claim_text: October 2025 Joint Evaluation Agreement with Samsung SDI and BMW AG to develop a demonstration vehicle with all-solid-state batteries.
scores.supports: Both counterparties are foreign filers (Samsung SDI -- Korean; BMW AG -- German). EDGAR fulltext search for 'Samsung SDI' returns 50 hits in 10-K/10-Q/20-F since 2024 but cannot independently confirm Solid Power role. Press-release-style disclosure: 'Joint Evaluation Agreement' is below JDA in stage hierarchy.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='Samsung SDI' = 50 hits since 2024 (broad); search for combined 'Solid Power' + 'Samsung SDI' shows only Solid Power's own filings.
scores.M_value: 0 independent SEC corroboration -- but both counterparties are foreign filers (Korean / German), so absence is expected. Foreign-issuer caveat partially applies.
scores.interpretation: Stage ladder: 'Joint Evaluation Agreement' (Oct 2025) sits BELOW a JDA, BELOW A-sample / B-sample / C-sample, and far below SOP. Solid Power supplies electrolyte; Samsung SDI fabricates cells; BMW determines pass/fail. Demonstration vehicle, not SOP. Calibration Heuristic 3 (extra weight): conflating evaluation agreement with commercialization milestone = MODERATE. Marketing as 'meaningful progress on our path towards commercialization' is overstatement of stage.

scores.claim_text: $50M DOE Assistance Agreement under BIL/IIJA for continuous sulfide electrolyte manufacturing line; $60M Solid Power cost share.
scores.supports: USAspending.gov confirms 4 DOE grants to SOLID POWER OPERATING, INC including a $50,000,000 award (DEMS0000122) from Department of Energy. Also confirmed: DEAR0001727 ($5.6M ARPA-E), DEEE0009189 ($3.6M EERE), DEEE0008861 ($1M EERE).
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_grants recipient_name='Solid Power' -> 4 awards totaling $60.2M, all DOE, including $50M assistance agreement matching claim.
scores.M_value: DOE grants confirmed: $50M (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law / IIJA -- matches DEMS prefix), $5.6M ARPA-E, $3.6M EERE, $1M EERE. Recipient name SOLID POWER OPERATING, INC.
scores.interpretation: Strong external corroboration on the only registry-verifiable claim. Grant income recognition pace ($3.1M received in 2025 against $50M total) is consistent with early-construction phase. PASS.

scores.claim_text: 24 issued US patents, 100 pending US applications, 111 non-US/PCT patents and applications as of Feb 1, 2026.
scores.supports: USPTO Open Data Portal: 'Solid Power' returns 189 total applications and 13 granted patents; 'Solid Power Operating' returns 165 applications and 6 granted. Recent grant + filing activity heavily concentrated in solid-state, electrolyte, sulfide, cathode, and battery/cell categories per sampled titles (e.g., 'COMPOSITE MATERIALS FOR USE IN CATHODE LAYERS,' 'FLEXIBLE FRAME FOR USE IN APPLYING HIGH PRESSURE IN THE MANUFACTURE OF A SOLID-STATE BATTERY CELL,' 'CARBON-RICH STRUCTURES FOR SUPPRESSION OF THERMAL RUNAWAY').
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee assignee_name='Solid Power' -> 189 applications, 13 granted. Most recent app filings 2025-09 through 2025-11 indicate active prosecution. Title categorization on sample of 15 recent: 4 solid-state, 5 cathode, 2 electrolyte, 1 sulfide, 9 battery/cell.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=189, n_granted=13 (USPTO ODP); claimed 24 issued US patents includes pre-2018 grants not visible to USPTO ODP search window for this assignee variant. Tech-area concentration is clearly battery/electrolyte (Calibration Heuristic 8: PASS threshold met).
scores.interpretation: n_granted >=10 with strong claimed-technology hits (sulfide / electrolyte / cathode / solid-state / battery). Not a Nikola pattern. The 24 vs 13 discrepancy is plausibly due to USPTO ODP indexing only post-2018 first-applicant filings and exclusive licenses from CU Boulder / Oak Ridge counting toward the 24. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Continuous electrolyte production pilot line to be commissioned by end of 2026; 75 MT/yr capacity; aspirational ROK partner facility up to 500 MT/yr.
scores.supports: EPA FRS confirms 3 EPA-registered SLDP facilities in Colorado (Louisville HQ pilot site; Thornton facility; Site II in Broomfield) -- physical pilot infrastructure exists. DOE grant ($50M) co-funds the continuous line.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities facility_name='Solid Power' state_abbr='CO' -> 3 facilities (SOLID POWER - 486 S. PIERCE AVE Louisville; SOLID POWER - THORNTON FACILITY 14902 Grant St; SOLID POWER SITE II Broomfield 14902 Grant St Ste 140).
scores.M_value: 3 EPA-regulated CO facilities (Louisville, Thornton, Broomfield) -- pilot infrastructure exists per EPA FRS. The 500 MT/yr Korean facility is explicitly 'pursue a potential partnership' -- no partner named, no site selected.
scores.interpretation: Pilot existence is verified by EPA FRS. However, two-stage claim: (a) 75 MT/yr continuous line by end-2026 = aspirational but supported by funded equipment ordering (PASS); (b) 500 MT/yr Korean facility = pure forward projection with no named partner, no permits, no site. Apply Calibration Heuristic 3 to (b): planned-vs-operational gap is wide. Net = MODERATE for the combined claim.

scores.claim_text: 2025 revenue $21.7M = $6.0M government + $15.8M collaborative (primarily SK On milestone work); BMW related-party revenue collapsed $5.41M -> $0.189M (-96% YoY); $122.6M operating loss; $274.9M accumulated deficit.
scores.supports: Audited financial statements -- not disputed. Calibration Heuristic 11 (battery-specific revenue recognition pattern): the entire 2025 revenue base is JDA / line-installation milestone revenue + DOE grant, NOT series-production commercial revenue. BMW related-party revenue down 96% YoY is a material negative signal.
scores.M_check: Audited financials cross-referenced against Note 'Related Party Transactions' for BMW. No M-source independent of company filings can corroborate revenue quality classification.
scores.M_value: $15.8M collaborative revenue, primarily SK On (foreign related party that holds equity); $6.0M government grant; $0.189M BMW related-party (collapsed from $5.41M). Accumulated deficit $274.9M against ~12-month cash burn ~$73M.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 11 + Calibration Heuristic 4: revenue is overwhelmingly (a) milestone-based development services from OEM/Tier-1 partners that are ALSO equity investors (SK On invested $30M at de-SPAC; BMW holds >5% and board seat), and (b) DOE grant. There is essentially NO commercial-product revenue. The 96% YoY collapse in BMW revenue, combined with Ford wind-down (C2), suggests the JDA-monetization phase is contracting before commercial-supply phase has begun. SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Total liquidity $336.5M at 12/31/2025; ATM $88.8M net in 2025 (avg $5.06/sh); $122.2M Registered Direct Offering Jan 2026; buyback at $1.05/sh avg in 2025.
scores.supports: Audited financials -- liquidity is substantively real. However, the $1.05/sh buyback average (2025) vs $5.06/sh ATM price (2025) is internally inconsistent: it implies the stock traded in a 5x+ range during the year, with the buyback happening at lows and the ATM at highs. This is highly unusual capital allocation.
scores.M_check: No external M-source check needed -- audited financials. Calibration Heuristic 10 (distress fingerprints): no Form 15-12G or going-concern, but ATM + Registered Direct + reverse-split-adjacent share count behavior would warrant monitoring.
scores.M_value: $336.5M liquidity + $122.2M post-cutoff raise = $458.7M cash runway against $73M annual cash burn ~= 6 years runway. NOT a near-term distress scenario.
scores.interpretation: Two competing signals: (a) liquidity is strong with multi-year runway (PASS-leaning), (b) buyback at $1.05 vs ATM at $5.06 is an opportunistic dilution-at-rallies pattern that, while not distress, is a signature of perceived-share-price-management at a pre-revenue speculative name. Net = MODERATE -- raising capital at every available window in advance of a 6+ year runway is more consistent with future dilution-at-need than confidence.

scores.claim_text: BMW Group i7 test vehicle featuring Solid Power cells unveiled May 2025 -- 'significant achievement in our partnership.'
scores.supports: Per Calibration Heuristic 5: NHTSA registers complete vehicles, not battery suppliers -- correct M-source choice would be the OEM's annual report (BMW AG, foreign filer with no SEC 20-F coverage). BMW's foreign-issuer status creates an unverifiability floor.
scores.M_check: NHTSA query for SLDP is non-applicable per catalog calibration guidance. EDGAR fulltext for 'Solid Power' in BMW filings: BMW AG is a German foreign issuer not filing with SEC EDGAR; no test-vehicle disclosure pathway via US filings.
scores.M_value: UNVERIFIABLE by US registry sources; demonstration / test vehicle stage is below SOP by 3-5 stages on the stage ladder.
scores.interpretation: A test vehicle is a demonstrator, NOT a production design-win. Stage ladder: test vehicle ~ B-sample / C-sample stage. Conflating test-vehicle reveal with commercialization progress is the central evasion pattern per Calibration Heuristic 3. Combined with the JDA's now-active termination rights (Dec 31, 2025) and 96% BMW-revenue collapse (C8), the test vehicle reads more as showcase than commitment. MODERATE.
